# Cross-Platform Benchmarks

[Home](../../../README.md) · [All categories](../../README.md) · [简体中文](cross-platform-benchmarks_cn.md)

Manipulation Action Models → Common Methods → Cross-Platform Benchmarks

Benchmarks whose main contribution is reusable evaluation across manipulation platforms, including coding agents and long-horizon execution. Record the evaluated systems, tasks, controller access, grading and budgets; distinguish paper evaluations from later platform support and cross-arm transfer from cross-hand transfer. Data generation and policy training remain secondary contributions within one record.

| [AM.MAN.METHOD.BENCH.1] <a id="am-man-method-bench-1"></a> | **EmbodiedSWE｜Coding Agent evaluation · Long-horizon manipulation · Demonstration generation**<br>[EmbodiedSWE: Coding Agents for Long Horizon Dexterous Robotics](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.27308v2)<br>Zeyu Shen, Haoxiang You, Yilang Liu, Zhicheng Zheng, Lihan Zha, Kashu Yamazaki, Mingtong Zhang, Suning Huang, Jiankai Sun, Qianzhong Chen, Lucy He, Kaiyuan Liu, Haoran Chang, Katerina Fragkiadaki, Dhruv Shah, Mac Schwager, Peter Henderson, Ian Abraham, Canwen Xu<br>**Tags:** `benchmark` `agent-benchmark` `coding-agent` `long-horizon-evaluation` `cross-embodiment` `cross-arm-transfer` `simulation` `isaac-lab` `programmatic-policy` `demonstration-generation` `verified-trajectory-generation` `agent-aided-diversification` [vla](../../topics/vla.md) `imitation-learning` `sim-to-real` `coding-agent-rl` | **Hands:** Paper v2 lists five embodiments: Franka with a two-finger parallel gripper, xArm7 with a linkage or Panda gripper, Kinova Gen3 with a Panda gripper, bimanual Franka with parallel grippers, and G1 with two three-finger hands. Hardware VLA uses Franka with Robotiq 2F-85. The current project advertises 17 embodiments; this does not establish equivalent paper evaluation of all later additions.<br>**Tasks:** Twenty-eight tasks cover assembly (9), packing (4), puzzles (6), deformables/liquids (4), cutting (2) and loco-manipulation (3), with physical execution horizons up to about 30 minutes. Agents submit solve(env) programs under a four-hour development budget per task in the main comparison, evaluated through independent hidden grading, success, time and cost. The benchmark is not a full 28-task-by-all-embodiment evaluation matrix.<br>**Same-task cross-hand reuse:** On six tasks, verified Franka programs serve as hints for Kinova Gen3 and xArm7. All three carry the Panda gripper, testing cross-arm program adaptation rather than cross-hand policy sharing. Other effectors such as G1 hands have task support, but matched zero-shot shared-policy validation across all hand morphologies is not reported.<br>**Release:** Official GitHub releases the benchmark, agent evaluation, EmbodiedSWE-Gen and VLA training/evaluation code; Hugging Face provides task and scene simulation assets. Execution is based on Isaac Lab, with Newton for the deformable suite. Downloads of complete generated demonstration datasets and trained VLA/agent checkpoints remain unverified; the asset collection is not a demonstration dataset.<br>**Key distinction:** EmbodiedSWE benchmarks coding-agent program synthesis and cross-task/cross-embodiment transfer on 28 long-horizon simulated robotics tasks, then expands successful programs into VLA demonstrations, linking program-solving evaluation to verified training data through independent grading and replay checks.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Solver agents inspect full simulator state and debug programs using generic IK/operational-space controllers; independent graders disable object-state writes. Privileged-state solver results are not vision-only policy results. Gen diversifies scenes, strategies, intermediate phases, dynamics and appearance, retaining successful replay-verified trajectories. Simulated SmolVLA experiments cover only six tasks, taking multi-view RGB, instructions and 8-D joint/gripper state to joint targets. Some success criteria are relaxed relative to the original benchmark, precluding direct comparison with full 28-task agent results. Hardware lamp disassembly finetunes π₀.₅-DROID on 500 simulation demonstrations without real demonstrations for finetuning; final bulb unscrewing/extraction succeeds in 20% of ten trials, with checkpoint selection based on hardware performance. A separate study PPO-post-trains a coding agent on 400 generated environments without completed held-out evaluation; this RL is not the main VLA action-learning procedure. | arXiv v2 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.27308v2) · [Project](https://embodiedswe.github.io/) · [Code](https://github.com/EmbodiedSWE/EmbodiedSWE) · [Assets](https://huggingface.co/datasets/EmbodiedSWE/robobench-assets) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-27 |
